title: Selecting and Managing Runner Environments knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Selecting and Managing Runner Environments?
options: Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
Pin runtime versions, install required tools reproducibly, and test the intended OS and architecture rather than relying on an unqualified runner label alone.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
questions.answer_key: Pin runtime versions, install required tools reproducibly, and test the intended OS and architecture rather than relying on an unqualified runner label alone.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of selecting and managing runner environments: Pin runtime versions, install required tools reproducibly, and test the intended OS and architecture rather than relying on an unqualified runner label alone. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to selecting and managing runner environments?
options: Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: Pin runtime versions, install required tools reproducibly, and test the intended OS and architecture rather than relying on an unqualified runner label alone. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
